episodes.title: Where Did Democracy Come From, and Does It Still Work?
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Political Theory, we’ll learn democracy has had its fair share of critics, past and present.

episodes.title: What Does Liberalism Mean?
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Political Theory, we learn the fundamentals of Classical Liberalism and how 17th-century philosophers impact politics today.

episodes.title: Identity Politics: The Good, The Bad, And The… Hotly Contested
episodes.description: Explore debates over whether governments should consider or disregard citizens’ identities.

episodes.title: What Are the Rules of War? Just War Theory
episodes.description: Consider when war can be justified and how just war theory evaluates armed conflict.

episodes.title: What does Machiavellian mean?
episodes.description: Explore the relationship between effective leadership and morality through Machiavelli’s political thought.

episodes.title: Who Was Karl Marx? And Why Is Everyone Still Talking About Him?
episodes.description: Examine Marx’s ideas about capitalism and communism beyond competing modern portrayals of Marxism.

episodes.title: A World Without Governments? Anarchism Explained
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Political Theory, we explore the theories and practices of anarchism.

episodes.title: What Does Feminism Stand For?
episodes.description: Explore the meaning of feminism in the twenty-first century.

episodes.title: Political Cosmopolitanism
episodes.description: Consider political cosmopolitanism and our obligations to people beyond our immediate communities.

episodes.title: Philosophies of Punishment & The Prison Abolition Movement
episodes.description: Explore the history behind mass incarceration and arguments made by the prison abolition movement.

episodes.title: Is Utopia Actually Possible?
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Political Theory, we’ll explore visions of utopia from Plato to bell hooks.

episodes.title: Should Art Be Political?
episodes.description: Explore how artists shape political perceptions and how political authorities attempt to control their influence.

episodes.title: The Power of Political Recognition
episodes.description: Trace political recognition from nineteenth-century philosophy to contemporary Native land acknowledgements, and consider whether recognition alone is sufficient.
